reference.title: Typing a date
reference.shortdesc: What uFTi reads when you type a date in one box, and what it keeps exactly as you typed it.

section.title: Plain words
section.p: Choose to type a whole date. Write it in words, with the day first, then the month, then the year. The box shows an example. Capital letters do not matter. You can write a month in full or with its first three letters.

row.entry: A date that is close, or that you worked out.
The earliest and the latest date it could be.
Something that lasted for a while.
A year before the common era. BCE works too.
A date in the Julian calendar. Name the calendar first.
A date with a dual year ().
The year 1700, with the word Easter kept beside it.

section.title: What uFTi keeps as you typed it
section.p: These are not read as dates. uFTi keeps them exactly as you typed them. It does not use them to order your events.

ul.li: 15/03/1900 and 03/04/1900. Countries put the day and the month in a different order, so uFTi does not guess.
c. 1850 and circa 1850. Write about 1850 instead.

section.title: Check the line that says Reads as
section.p: When uFTi cannot read a date, it does not stop you, and it does not warn you. The line under the box only repeats what you typed, such as Reads as Easter 1700. So read that line each time. For a date that uFTi has understood, the line shows it in words, such as Reads as 15 March 1900.
A date that cannot be read stays in the box as text. stays on for it, because the day, month and year pickers cannot show it.
